expectations.evidence: The document only mentions VS-NfD repeatedly but never names the other German classification levels (VS-VERTRAULICH, GEHEIM, STRENG GEHEIM). There is no enumeration or explanation of the classification hierarchy.

Section 13 provides detailed coverage of IT-Grundschutz methodology including: Schutzbedarfsfeststellung (protection needs assessment), building blocks (Bausteine) with specific IDs, the requirement to implement BASIS/STANDARD/high-protection requirements, supplementary risk analysis per BSI Standard 200-3, and modeling in verinice. Section 13.3 explains the multi-step process agencies must follow.

Section 14 explains C5 in detail: 17 categories with ~121 criteria, the Type 1 (point-in-time design assessment) and Type 2 (operating effectiveness over 6-12 months) attestation phases, the preparation phase including gap analysis and engaging a Wirtschaftspruefungsgesellschaft, and annual renewal requirement.

Section 8 provides a comprehensive layer-by-layer decision matrix distinguishing where BSI-approved products are mandatory (perimeter firewalls, VPN gateways, HSMs, TPMs) vs where FLOSS is acceptable (OS, hypervisor, OpenStack services, internal encryption, SIEM, backup). Specific approved products are named (genugate, SINA Box, genuconnect, Utimaco HSMs).

Section 9.1 specifically addresses BSI TR-02102-1 and TR-02102-2 with a detailed table of compliant algorithms and key lengths. BSI preference for Brainpool curves over NIST curves is noted. Section 2.2 lists BSI TR-02102, TR-03116, TL-03402, TR-03107, TR-02103. Appendix B provides BSI TR-02102-2 compliant TLS cipher suite configuration.

Section 2.3 explicitly states: 'All data must be stored and processed within Germany (no exceptions)', 'Data centers must be on German soil, operated by security-cleared German personnel', 'No foreign intelligence service (FISA, Cloud Act, etc.) jurisdiction may apply', and 'Network traffic carrying VS-NfD data must not leave German territory'. DSGVO/BDSG are listed in the regulatory framework table.

Section 13.1 lists dozens of specific Bausteine (building blocks) organized by category (ISMS, ORP, CON, OPS, DER, APP, SYS, NET, INF) with their German titles. Section 13.2 covers Schutzbedarfsfeststellung with protection level tables. Section 13.3 describes the full methodology: Strukturanalyse, modeling the Informationsverbund in verinice, implementing Anforderungen at BASIS/STANDARD/high-protection levels, and supplementary risk analysis per BSI Standard 200-3.

Section 8 provides a detailed decision framework (8.1) with four tiers: zugelassenes Produkt (mandatory BSI-approved), zertifiziertes Produkt (BSI/CC certified strongly recommended), BSI-evaluated (FLOSS acceptable with hardening), and neither (FLOSS with risk assessment). Section 8.2 has a 16-row table analyzing each layer individually. Section 8.3 summarizes the five mandatory non-FLOSS components.

Section 13.1 maps specific Grundschutz building blocks to OpenStack components (SYS.1.5 for virtualization/hypervisor, SYS.1.8 for Ceph storage, NET.1.1 for network architecture, OPS.2.2 for cloud usage). Section 8.2 confirms OpenStack services have no BSI approval requirement but must be hardened per Grundschutz. The architecture explicitly maps OpenStack zones to Grundschutz network architecture requirements (NET.1.1).

The document does not mention NIS2, EUCS (EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme), or ENISA. It references GDPR/DSGVO but treats it purely as a German requirement. The framework is presented entirely within a national German context with no discussion of how it relates to broader EU cybersecurity directives or certification schemes.

Section 15.1 provides a detailed month-by-month timeline from foundation (Month 1-3) through VS-NfD Freigabe (Month 18-24) and explicitly addresses ongoing requirements: annual C5 Type 2 re-attestation, triennial ISO 27001 re-certification, continuous monitoring, and regular BSI coordination meetings. Section 15.2 covers critical success factors including early BSI engagement (Vorabstimmung) and the ongoing nature of compliance.

The document is thoroughly German-centric. DISA STIG is mentioned only once as a parenthetical note about OS hardening availability alongside the BSI SiSyPHuS profile (not as a primary standard). There is no mention of FedRAMP, IL levels, or NIST SP publications. All primary frameworks are German (BSI IT-Grundschutz, C5, VSA, BSI TR series). The minor STIG mention is informational, not prescriptive.
